newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rise to all-time high, pull back.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rise to all-time high, pull back.

text.p: French stocks rose to all time highs in early trading on Monday but then pulled back to wait for the outcome of a meeting of European leaders in Amsterdam.

The bourse's blue-chip CAC-40 index rose to an all time high of 2,825.18 points, bolstered by record gains on Wall Street and expectations an accord would be reached in Amsterdam, but then slid back to 2,801.15 at 0930 GMT, down 0.26 percent.

European leaders are expected to try to accommodate France's Socialist-led government by offering vague language stressing the importance of creating jobs in the European monetary union without making the kind of changes to the stability pact on fiscal discipline that would upset Germany.
No agreement was reached at a Franco-German summit on Friday in the French city of Poitiers.
"Everything's suspended as the market watches for declarations from Amsterdam. If expectations for an accord fade, the market could go down sharply," a broker said.
Shares in Eurotunnel rose 3.10 percent at 6.65 francs after the Shuttle freight service, damaged by fire last year, resumed on schedule on Sunday.
Weakness persisted in defence stocks on concerns that the sector's restructuring may be delayed. Dassault Aviation's stock fell 0.75 percent and Thomson-CSF shares were down 0.51 percent.
Dassault chairman Serge Dassault stressed at the Paris air show that it was crucial to allow the French industry to take part in the consolidation of the European aerospace sector.

He said he remained in favour of a merger between Dassault Aviation and state-owned Aerospatiale on the condition that the merged group be privatised immediately. He said he could accept the state holding on to as much as 49 percent.
